But 'clause 8.3(b)' and 'section 8.3(b)' may not be close if the model hasn't seen this exact identifier pattern. BM25 exact-match search trivially finds 'clause 8.3(b)' as a term match. Hybrid RAG = BM25 results + dense results, fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion: score = 1/(k+rank_BM25) + 1/(k+rank_dense). The RRF score promotes documents that rank well in either system. This is a standard finding: dense search for semantic queries, BM25 for IDs/codes/names/version numbers.

questions.prompt: Explain end-to-end how ChatGPT works — from user typing a message to receiving a response. Cover: tokenization, the Transformer forward pass, KV cache, pretraining, SFT, and RLHF. You have 8 minutes.

rubric.criterion: Tokenization: text → BPE token IDs → embedding lookup + RoPE positional encoding
Transformer forward pass: multi-head causal self-attention (Q/K/V, scaled dot product, causal mask) → residual → RMSNorm → FFN (SwiGLU) → residual — repeated 96× (GPT-4 scale)
Output: final layer → linear projection to vocab size → softmax → temperature scaling → sampling (greedy/top-p/top-k) → next token; KV cache stores all K/V from prior tokens to avoid recomputation
Pretraining: trained on trillions of tokens with next-token prediction loss; cross-entropy loss → backprop → AdamW weight updates; causal masking ensures no future token leakage
Alignment pipeline: SFT on demonstration data → reward model trained on (chosen, rejected) preference pairs → PPO/DPO to maximize reward while staying close to SFT model (KL penalty)
Connects the components coherently — pretraining gives world knowledge, SFT teaches format, RLHF/DPO aligns behavior to be helpful/harmless

questions.modelAnswer: 1. USER INPUT: 'What is the capital of France?' → GPT-4 tokenizer (BPE) → [1867, 374, 279, 6864, 315, 9822, 30] token IDs. 2. EMBEDDING: each ID → 12288-dim vector via embedding table; RoPE adds position rotation to Q and K. 3. FORWARD PASS (×96 layers): Multi-head attention (96 heads, causal mask) → Q·Kᵀ/√128 → softmax → ×V → project → residual + RMSNorm → SwiGLU FFN (expand to 49152, gate, contract back to 12288) → residual + RMSNorm. KV cache stores all prior K,V tensors — only new token's Q is computed each step. 4. OUTPUT: last layer → linear (12288→100k vocab) → softmax → temperature 0.7 → top-p 0.9 sampling → token ID → decode to 'Paris'. 5. PRETRAINING: GPT-4 base trained on ~13T tokens with causal LM loss; AdamW, cosine schedule, 25k warmup steps — learns world knowledge. 6. SFT: supervised fine-tuning on 13k human-written prompt-response pairs → model learns instruction-following format. 7. REWARD MODEL: human labelers rank 4 responses; Bradley-Terry model trained on (chosen, rejected) pairs. 8. RLHF (PPO): policy model generates responses, reward model scores them, PPO updates policy to maximize reward while KL penalty keeps it close to SFT model. Result: ChatGPT = helpful, harmless, honest assistant.

questions.prompt: Why does speculative decoding (draft + verify) speed up LLM inference despite running two models?

options.text: The draft model is faster than the large model, so total compute is reduced

LLM decoding is memory-bandwidth bound, not compute bound — verifying K draft tokens in one large model pass costs the same as generating 1 token, but accepts 2-4 tokens on average, multiplying throughput
Speculative decoding uses int4 quantization for both models, reducing memory reads
The draft model's tokens are always accepted — rejection only applies to tokens with probability < 0.1

questions.explanation: Autoregressive LLM decoding is limited by memory bandwidth, not arithmetic compute — reading model weights from HBM is the bottleneck. The large model's forward pass takes nearly the same wall-clock time whether it processes 1 token or K tokens (up to a batch size limit), because the memory reads dominate. Speculative decoding exploits this: draft model (7B) proposes 4 tokens → large model (70B) verifies all 4 in one pass. If 3 are accepted, you get 3 tokens for the cost of 1 large-model pass — roughly 3× throughput. The output distribution is provably identical to sampling from the large model alone.
